title: Build log | Krishnendu Biswas
description: What I build and run with agents, reviewed before publishing.

items.title: Rebuilt this site; fact audit checked every number
items.summary: This site went from a game-themed page to a professional portfolio. A planning model wrote the spec, a builder agent worked through it from a task board, and served screenshots were reviewed before it went live. The diagrams and charts are now 14 inline SVG figures, each with a data table.
items.content_html:
What changed: This site went from a game-themed page to a professional portfolio. A planning model wrote the spec, a builder agent worked through it from a task board, and served screenshots were reviewed before it went live. The diagrams and charts are now 14 inline SVG figures, each with a data table.

Why it matters: Every number on the site now traces to a source line: 380 numbers in all. A script measures diagram text on 23 pages at 3 screen widths. Rows under the 13px floor went from 18 to 0.

Result: Merged and live on 3 Oct 2026, with 0 failing rows on the text size check.

Lesson: An earlier draft contained claims that did not match my records, and the fact audit caught them before release. An automated review also passed a build with visible defects, so every release now gets a separate check of the rendered pages before it goes live.

Sources: Task card: v2 visual redesign with diagrams and charts, including the reviewer run and the model fallback, Task card: v2.1 diagram polish, facts map and diagram text size check, Task card: v1.2 agent case studies, where the unmatched claims were found

items.title: Moved the agents from laptop to cloud server
items.summary: Hermes Agent, the open-source framework my agents run on, moved from a Linux virtual machine on my MacBook (M1 Max) to a cloud server running Ubuntu. The model gateway (9Router, which sends each request to a model) and the provider sync now run as system services on that server.
items.content_html:
What changed: Hermes Agent, the open-source framework my agents run on, moved from a Linux virtual machine on my MacBook (M1 Max) to a cloud server running Ubuntu. The model gateway (9Router, which sends each request to a model) and the provider sync now run as system services on that server.

Why it matters: The agents keep working when the laptop is closed. Scheduled jobs and the daily progress report no longer depend on my machine being awake.

Result: Gateway and sync were deployed as services on 21 Sep 2026.

Lesson: The date of this move rests on a billing record and a boot log rather than my memory. I now log every milestone to an append-only ledger with an ID before I write about it.

Sources: Ledger: first billed day of the cloud server (billing record, amount withheld), Ledger: cloud server first boot, from the system boot log, Ledger: agent runtime moved from laptop to cloud server, Ledger: model gateway and provider sync deployed as system services
